article_ideas.angle: Trace the engineering surface shift from test-time search orchestration to pretraining-data and prior curation, and argue that teams that keep investing in tuning infrastructure are investing in the part that is being deleted.

article_ideas.title: The Pipeline Was the Product: What Happens to ML Engineering When the Algorithm Is Pretrained

article_ideas.angle: Compare direct context stuffing against a tool-call route on cost, latency, and accuracy, and derive a routing rule for when a modality belongs behind a tool boundary rather than inside the context window.

article_ideas.title: Stop Stuffing Tables Into Context: Tool Boundaries as the Correct Architecture for Structured Data Agents

article_ideas.angle: Use TabNet as the canonical case for a general adoption checklist: which evaluation protocols would have flagged the failure before deployment, and how to apply that checklist to the next architecture that claims to replace boosted trees.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Prof. Frank Hutter (and Tim/host)
  • Channel: Machine Learning Street Talk
  • Main topic: TabPFN and Tabular Foundation Models
  • Purpose: To explain the mechanics, theoretical grounding, benchmark performance, and enterprise applications of tabular foundation models like TabPFN. Prof. Frank Hutter discusses TabPFN, a transformer-based tabular foundation model developed by Prior Labs that replaces traditional AutoML pipelines and hyperparameter tuning with a single forward pass. The conversation explores why tabular data is difficult for deep learning, the transition from traditional ML methods to in-context learning foundation models, scalability improvements in TabPFN v2, v2.5, v3, and v3.5, the inclusion of causal reasoning and relational data, and comparisons with LLMs.

Topic Map

Why Tabular Data Resisted Deep Learning

  • Explanation: Tabular data is messy, heterogeneous, contains missing values, outliers, and categorical/binary variables. Standard deep learning architectures treat all inputs like images or text and fail to capture data complexities or invariances.
  • Key claims:
    • Traditional deep learning approaches like TabNet failed to generalize to new tabular data sets.
    • Tabular data has extreme heterogeneity and various data complexities that standard deep learning architectures mishandle.
    • Traditional machine learning requires a unique pipeline, infrastructure, and team per prediction task.
  • Examples:
    • Google's TabNet received thousands of citations but failed to generalize across new datasets.
    • Tabular tables have billions of tokens if thrown into LLMs, making LLMs million times too expensive, slow, and inaccurate.
  • Terminology:
    • TabNet
    • CatBoost
    • XGBoost
    • AutoML
    • in-context learning
    • tabular data
  • Why it matters: Tabular data is ubiquitous in science, medicine, finance, and enterprise, yet deep learning had historically failed to solve it effectively.

The Tabular ImageNet Moment: TabPFN

  • Explanation: TabPFN represents the natural progression of AutoML where an entire machine learning algorithm is learned via in-context learning and executed in a single forward pass.
  • Key claims:
    • TabPFN v2 performs dramatically better than CatBoost and XGBoost.
    • TabPFN learns the entire algorithm during meta-training on synthetic datasets generated from structural causal models.
    • It eliminates hyperparameters tuning and model selection at test time.
  • Examples:
    • TabPFN makes accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model published in Nature.
    • TabArena benchmark shows new waves of deep learning methods outperforming traditional boosted trees.
  • Terminology:
    • TabPFN
    • Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs)
    • TabArena
    • meta-training
  • Why it matters: It marks the exact moment deep learning successfully conquered tabular data, acting as the ImageNet moment for tabular prediction.

From AutoML to Learned Algorithms

  • Explanation: Frank Hutter reflects on his 15 years of research in automated machine learning, starting from automatic algorithm configuration (SMAC, Auto-WEKA) to hyperparameter optimization, and finally converging on foundation models.
  • Key claims:
    • Automated algorithm configuration required countless evaluations over complex hierarchical parameter spaces.
    • Foundation models collapse the complex pipeline search into a single forward pass.
    • Humans like to put text, images, and videos online, but tabular data is often proprietary and unglamorous.
  • Examples:
    • Auto-WEKA and SMAC for automated machine learning.
    • Decayed weight decay regularization and SGDR optimization papers with Ilya Loshchilov.
  • Terminology:
    • SMAC
    • Auto-WEKA
    • Hyperparameter optimization
    • Neural Architecture Search (NAS)
  • Why it matters: Traces the historical trajectory from manual ML pipelines to automated search, and ultimately to pre-trained foundation models.

Bayesian Prediction in One Forward Pass

  • Explanation: TabPFN approximates Bayesian inference over priors by meta-learning over structural causal models, enabling uncertainty estimation and robust predictions in a single forward pass.
  • Key claims:
    • TabPFN approximates Bayesian posterior over functions parameterized by latents.
    • Both MCMC and variational inference are slow and approximate, whereas PFNs compute approximations instantly via forward pass.
    • By synthesizing data from structural causal models, PFNs learn robust priors.
  • Examples:
    • Gaussian process priors and posterior predictive distributions.
    • Illustration of Prior-Data Fitted Networks sampling from structural causal models.
  • Terminology:
    • Bayesian inference
    • posterior predictive distribution
    • structural causal models (SCMs)
    • Gaussian processes
  • Why it matters: Provides exact or near-exact Bayesian uncertainty estimates without the computational bottleneck of traditional sampling methods.

Scaling Tables and Pairing PFNs with Agents

  • Explanation: Discusses scaling TabPFN to millions of rows, integrating it with AI agents via Model Context Protocol (MCP), and beating traditional baselines on living benchmarks like TabArena.
  • Key claims:
    • TabPFN-3 scales dataset sizes up to 1M training rows and supports relational and tabular-text data.
    • TabPFN MCP enables AI tools like Claude to make natural language predictions on tabular data.
    • TabArena is a living benchmark for machine learning on tabular data.
  • Examples:
    • TabPFN-3 beating all non-TabPFN models on TabArena leaderboard.
    • Hitachi preventive maintenance and CreditPlus credit risk assessment case studies.
  • Terminology:
    • TabArena
    • Model Context Protocol (MCP)
    • TabPFN-3
    • TabFM
    • TabCLV2
  • Why it matters: Demonstrates real-world utility, scalability to large industrial datasets, and agentic integration.

Heads, Rows, Columns and Complexity

  • Explanation: Examines the underlying architecture of TabPFN, alternating row and column attention, embedding strategies, and complexity trade-offs.
  • Key claims:
    • TabPFN v2 uses alternating row and column attention to capture interactions across rows and columns.
    • Complexity scales quadratically with rows and columns depending on the version.
    • Separating classification and regression heads is necessary because gradient propagation behaves differently.
  • Examples:
    • TabPFN v2 architecture showing 1-D feature attention and 1-D sample attention layers.
    • Table complexity scaling from n^2m + nm^2 in v2.
  • Terminology:
    • row attention
    • column attention
    • positional embedding
    • complexity
    • permutation equivariance
  • Why it matters: Explains the mathematical and architectural breakthroughs that allow transformers to operate efficiently on tabular data matrices.

Test-Time Adaptation and Extrapolation

  • Explanation: Explores test-time adaptation, finetuning on periodic signals, prompt-tuning, and the model's ability to extrapolate trends beyond the training data.
  • Key claims:
    • TabPFN-3 is able to extrapolate successfully, which traditional tree-based models struggle with.
    • Finetuning TabPFN on user-specific tabular datasets yields significant performance gains.
    • Prompt tuning allows context-aware feature engineering using LLMs.
  • Examples:
    • Finetunability of TabPFN on periodic signals.
    • Extrapolation behavior graphs comparing TabPFN-3 to CatBoost.
  • Terminology:
    • test-time adaptation
    • extrapolation
    • prompt tuning
    • CAAFE
  • Why it matters: Shows how models can adapt to out-of-distribution data and perform rigorous extrapolation.

Priors Are the Moat

  • Explanation: Google's TabFM cloned the PFN recipe and scaled it up, demonstrating that the secret sauce lies in the synthetic data generation and prior specification.
  • Key claims:
    • Google's TabFM adopted the PFN recipe and scaled it up 30 times.
    • Priors embedded during pre-training are the ultimate competitive moat for tabular foundation models.
    • Imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.
  • Examples:
    • Google Research's TabFM topping its own TabArena run.
    • TabFM borrowing the PFN recipe with alternating row and column attention.
  • Terminology:
    • TabFM
    • priors
    • moat
    • synthetic data
  • Why it matters: Validates the foundational paradigm shift while highlighting the commercial and intellectual property dynamics in foundation model research.

From Correlation to Intervention: Do-PFN

  • Explanation: Discusses causal discovery, causal effect estimation, and Do-PFN for making interventional predictions from purely observational data.
  • Key claims:
    • Do-PFN allows interventional predictions from standard observational data by pre-training on sampled structural causal models.
    • Observation is not intervention.
    • Causal effect estimation is critical for scientific disciplines, medicine, and economics.
  • Examples:
    • Do-PFN: In-Context Learning for Causal Effect Estimation paper.
    • Medical patient treatment intervention scenarios.
  • Terminology:
    • Do-PFN
    • causal effect estimation
    • interventional predictions
    • structural causal models
    • do-operator
  • Why it matters: Bridges machine learning and causal inference, enabling models to answer 'what if' questions rather than just correlations.

Causal Products and Enterprise Adoption

  • Explanation: Discusses commercialization, Prior Labs, open weights versus enterprise licensing, APIs, and real-world case studies like Hitachi and CreditPlus.
  • Key claims:
    • Prior Labs offers open weights with a non-commercial license and paid enterprise APIs for production.
    • TabPFN achieves 1st place on 7 different tabular-related benchmarks.
    • Hitachi and CreditPlus successfully deployed TabPFN for railway predictive maintenance and automotive finance credit risk.
  • Examples:
    • Hitachi predicting maintenance workflows across Spain's railway.
    • CreditPlus increasing loan approvals while keeping strict risk thresholds.
  • Terminology:
    • Prior Labs
    • API
    • open weights
    • enterprise licensing
    • preventive maintenance
  • Why it matters: Bridges academic research and commercial deployment, showing immediate industrial ROI.

Key Points

Tabular foundation models eliminate manual pipeline construction

  • Explanation: Traditional machine learning requires data cleaning, missing value imputation, feature engineering, and model selection. TabPFN handles all of this in a single forward pass.
  • Evidence: TabPFN outperforms tuned XGBoost and CatBoost while running orders of magnitude faster.
  • Practical implication: Data scientists can bypass tedious preprocessing and feature engineering, shifting their focus to framing problems correctly.

Synthetic data generation solves data scarcity for pre-training

  • Explanation: Because there are not enough diverse tabular datasets on the internet to train a foundation model, PFNs generate millions of synthetic datasets from structural causal models.
  • Evidence: Pre-training on synthetic structural causal models allows the transformer to learn rich Bayesian priors.
  • Practical implication: Enables training powerful foundation models from scratch without relying on web scraping.

Alternating row and column attention captures table geometry

  • Explanation: Tabular datasets have both row-level samples and column-level features. TabPFN applies alternating attention mechanisms over both dimensions.
  • Evidence: TabPFN v2 and v3 architectures utilize dedicated row and column attention modules.
  • Practical implication: Preserves permutation equivariance and models complex interactions across both rows and columns.

Causal pre-training enables interventional forecasting

  • Explanation: Standard ML models only learn correlations. By pre-training on structural causal models, Do-PFN can predict the outcomes of actions or interventions.
  • Evidence: Do-PFN paper demonstrates accurate causal effect estimation from observational data.
  • Practical implication: Allows decision-makers in medicine and finance to simulate interventions before executing them.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

TabPFN (Prior-Data Fitted Network)

  • How it works: Meta-learns an inference algorithm by pre-training a transformer on synthetic datasets sampled from a prior over functions, enabling in-context learning on new tabular datasets during a single forward pass.
  • Components:
    • Synthetic data generator (Structural Causal Models)
    • Transformer architecture with row and column attention
    • In-context learning engine
  • When to use: For any tabular classification or regression task, especially on small to medium-sized datasets where rapid deployment and zero hyperparameter tuning are desired.

Do-PFN

  • How it works: Extends PFNs to causal inference by generating training data from sampled structural causal models, simulating interventions, and learning to predict interventional targets.
  • Components:
    • Causal graph sampler
    • Intervention simulator
    • Transformer inference network
  • When to use: When estimating causal effects and predicting the consequences of interventions from observational data.

Examples & Case Studies

summary.markdown:
## Overview
- **Speaker**: Prof. Frank Hutter (and Tim/host)
- **Channel**: Machine Learning Street Talk
- **Main topic**: TabPFN and Tabular Foundation Models
- **Purpose**: To explain the mechanics, theoretical grounding, benchmark performance, and enterprise applications of tabular foundation models like TabPFN.
Prof. Frank Hutter discusses TabPFN, a transformer-based tabular foundation model developed by Prior Labs that replaces traditional AutoML pipelines and hyperparameter tuning with a single forward pass. The conversation explores why tabular data is difficult for deep learning, the transition from traditional ML methods to in-context learning foundation models, scalability improvements in TabPFN v2, v2.5, v3, and v3.5, the inclusion of causal reasoning and relational data, and comparisons with LLMs.
## Topic Map
### Why Tabular Data Resisted Deep Learning
- **Explanation**: Tabular data is messy, heterogeneous, contains missing values, outliers, and categorical/binary variables. Standard deep learning architectures treat all inputs like images or text and fail to capture data complexities or invariances.
- **Key claims**:
  - Traditional deep learning approaches like TabNet failed to generalize to new tabular data sets.
  - Tabular data has extreme heterogeneity and various data complexities that standard deep learning architectures mishandle.
  - Traditional machine learning requires a unique pipeline, infrastructure, and team per prediction task.
- **Examples**:
  - Google's TabNet received thousands of citations but failed to generalize across new datasets.
  - Tabular tables have billions of tokens if thrown into LLMs, making LLMs million times too expensive, slow, and inaccurate.
- **Terminology**:
  - TabNet
  - CatBoost
  - XGBoost
  - AutoML
  - in-context learning
  - tabular data
- **Why it matters**: Tabular data is ubiquitous in science, medicine, finance, and enterprise, yet deep learning had historically failed to solve it effectively.
### The Tabular ImageNet Moment: TabPFN
- **Explanation**: TabPFN represents the natural progression of AutoML where an entire machine learning algorithm is learned via in-context learning and executed in a single forward pass.
- **Key claims**:
  - TabPFN v2 performs dramatically better than CatBoost and XGBoost.
  - TabPFN learns the entire algorithm during meta-training on synthetic datasets generated from structural causal models.
  - It eliminates hyperparameters tuning and model selection at test time.
- **Examples**:
  - TabPFN makes accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model published in Nature.
  - TabArena benchmark shows new waves of deep learning methods outperforming traditional boosted trees.
- **Terminology**:
  - TabPFN
  - Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs)
  - TabArena
  - meta-training
- **Why it matters**: It marks the exact moment deep learning successfully conquered tabular data, acting as the ImageNet moment for tabular prediction.
### From AutoML to Learned Algorithms
- **Explanation**: Frank Hutter reflects on his 15 years of research in automated machine learning, starting from automatic algorithm configuration (SMAC, Auto-WEKA) to hyperparameter optimization, and finally converging on foundation models.
- **Key claims**:
  - Automated algorithm configuration required countless evaluations over complex hierarchical parameter spaces.
  - Foundation models collapse the complex pipeline search into a single forward pass.
  - Humans like to put text, images, and videos online, but tabular data is often proprietary and unglamorous.
- **Examples**:
  - Auto-WEKA and SMAC for automated machine learning.
  - Decayed weight decay regularization and SGDR optimization papers with Ilya Loshchilov.
- **Terminology**:
  - SMAC
  - Auto-WEKA
  - Hyperparameter optimization
  - Neural Architecture Search (NAS)
- **Why it matters**: Traces the historical trajectory from manual ML pipelines to automated search, and ultimately to pre-trained foundation models.
### Bayesian Prediction in One Forward Pass
- **Explanation**: TabPFN approximates Bayesian inference over priors by meta-learning over structural causal models, enabling uncertainty estimation and robust predictions in a single forward pass.
- **Key claims**:
  - TabPFN approximates Bayesian posterior over functions parameterized by latents.
  - Both MCMC and variational inference are slow and approximate, whereas PFNs compute approximations instantly via forward pass.
  - By synthesizing data from structural causal models, PFNs learn robust priors.
- **Examples**:
  - Gaussian process priors and posterior predictive distributions.
  - Illustration of Prior-Data Fitted Networks sampling from structural causal models.
- **Terminology**:
  - Bayesian inference
  - posterior predictive distribution
  - structural causal models (SCMs)
  - Gaussian processes
- **Why it matters**: Provides exact or near-exact Bayesian uncertainty estimates without the computational bottleneck of traditional sampling methods.
### Scaling Tables and Pairing PFNs with Agents
- **Explanation**: Discusses scaling TabPFN to millions of rows, integrating it with AI agents via Model Context Protocol (MCP), and beating traditional baselines on living benchmarks like TabArena.
- **Key claims**:
  - TabPFN-3 scales dataset sizes up to 1M training rows and supports relational and tabular-text data.
  - TabPFN MCP enables AI tools like Claude to make natural language predictions on tabular data.
  - TabArena is a living benchmark for machine learning on tabular data.
- **Examples**:
  - TabPFN-3 beating all non-TabPFN models on TabArena leaderboard.
  - Hitachi preventive maintenance and CreditPlus credit risk assessment case studies.
- **Terminology**:
  - TabArena
  - Model Context Protocol (MCP)
  - TabPFN-3
  - TabFM
  - TabCLV2
- **Why it matters**: Demonstrates real-world utility, scalability to large industrial datasets, and agentic integration.
### Heads, Rows, Columns and Complexity
- **Explanation**: Examines the underlying architecture of TabPFN, alternating row and column attention, embedding strategies, and complexity trade-offs.
- **Key claims**:
  - TabPFN v2 uses alternating row and column attention to capture interactions across rows and columns.
  - Complexity scales quadratically with rows and columns depending on the version.
  - Separating classification and regression heads is necessary because gradient propagation behaves differently.
- **Examples**:
  - TabPFN v2 architecture showing 1-D feature attention and 1-D sample attention layers.
  - Table complexity scaling from n^2*m + n*m^2 in v2.
- **Terminology**:
  - row attention
  - column attention
  - positional embedding
  - complexity
  - permutation equivariance
- **Why it matters**: Explains the mathematical and architectural breakthroughs that allow transformers to operate efficiently on tabular data matrices.
### Test-Time Adaptation and Extrapolation
- **Explanation**: Explores test-time adaptation, finetuning on periodic signals, prompt-tuning, and the model's ability to extrapolate trends beyond the training data.
- **Key claims**:
  - TabPFN-3 is able to extrapolate successfully, which traditional tree-based models struggle with.
  - Finetuning TabPFN on user-specific tabular datasets yields significant performance gains.
  - Prompt tuning allows context-aware feature engineering using LLMs.
- **Examples**:
  - Finetunability of TabPFN on periodic signals.
  - Extrapolation behavior graphs comparing TabPFN-3 to CatBoost.
- **Terminology**:
  - test-time adaptation
  - extrapolation
  - prompt tuning
  - CAAFE
- **Why it matters**: Shows how models can adapt to out-of-distribution data and perform rigorous extrapolation.
### Priors Are the Moat
- **Explanation**: Google's TabFM cloned the PFN recipe and scaled it up, demonstrating that the secret sauce lies in the synthetic data generation and prior specification.
- **Key claims**:
  - Google's TabFM adopted the PFN recipe and scaled it up 30 times.
  - Priors embedded during pre-training are the ultimate competitive moat for tabular foundation models.
  - Imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.
- **Examples**:
  - Google Research's TabFM topping its own TabArena run.
  - TabFM borrowing the PFN recipe with alternating row and column attention.
- **Terminology**:
  - TabFM
  - priors
  - moat
  - synthetic data
- **Why it matters**: Validates the foundational paradigm shift while highlighting the commercial and intellectual property dynamics in foundation model research.
### From Correlation to Intervention: Do-PFN
- **Explanation**: Discusses causal discovery, causal effect estimation, and Do-PFN for making interventional predictions from purely observational data.
- **Key claims**:
  - Do-PFN allows interventional predictions from standard observational data by pre-training on sampled structural causal models.
  - Observation is not intervention.
  - Causal effect estimation is critical for scientific disciplines, medicine, and economics.
- **Examples**:
  - Do-PFN: In-Context Learning for Causal Effect Estimation paper.
  - Medical patient treatment intervention scenarios.
- **Terminology**:
  - Do-PFN
  - causal effect estimation
  - interventional predictions
  - structural causal models
  - do-operator
- **Why it matters**: Bridges machine learning and causal inference, enabling models to answer 'what if' questions rather than just correlations.
### Causal Products and Enterprise Adoption
- **Explanation**: Discusses commercialization, Prior Labs, open weights versus enterprise licensing, APIs, and real-world case studies like Hitachi and CreditPlus.
- **Key claims**:
  - Prior Labs offers open weights with a non-commercial license and paid enterprise APIs for production.
  - TabPFN achieves 1st place on 7 different tabular-related benchmarks.
  - Hitachi and CreditPlus successfully deployed TabPFN for railway predictive maintenance and automotive finance credit risk.
- **Examples**:
  - Hitachi predicting maintenance workflows across Spain's railway.
  - CreditPlus increasing loan approvals while keeping strict risk thresholds.
- **Terminology**:
  - Prior Labs
  - API
  - open weights
  - enterprise licensing
  - preventive maintenance
- **Why it matters**: Bridges academic research and commercial deployment, showing immediate industrial ROI.
## Key Points
### Tabular foundation models eliminate manual pipeline construction
- **Explanation**: Traditional machine learning requires data cleaning, missing value imputation, feature engineering, and model selection. TabPFN handles all of this in a single forward pass.
- **Evidence**: TabPFN outperforms tuned XGBoost and CatBoost while running orders of magnitude faster.
- **Practical implication**: Data scientists can bypass tedious preprocessing and feature engineering, shifting their focus to framing problems correctly.
### Synthetic data generation solves data scarcity for pre-training
- **Explanation**: Because there are not enough diverse tabular datasets on the internet to train a foundation model, PFNs generate millions of synthetic datasets from structural causal models.
- **Evidence**: Pre-training on synthetic structural causal models allows the transformer to learn rich Bayesian priors.
- **Practical implication**: Enables training powerful foundation models from scratch without relying on web scraping.
### Alternating row and column attention captures table geometry
- **Explanation**: Tabular datasets have both row-level samples and column-level features. TabPFN applies alternating attention mechanisms over both dimensions.
- **Evidence**: TabPFN v2 and v3 architectures utilize dedicated row and column attention modules.
- **Practical implication**: Preserves permutation equivariance and models complex interactions across both rows and columns.
### Causal pre-training enables interventional forecasting
- **Explanation**: Standard ML models only learn correlations. By pre-training on structural causal models, Do-PFN can predict the outcomes of actions or interventions.
- **Evidence**: Do-PFN paper demonstrates accurate causal effect estimation from observational data.
- **Practical implication**: Allows decision-makers in medicine and finance to simulate interventions before executing them.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### TabPFN (Prior-Data Fitted Network)
- **How it works**: Meta-learns an inference algorithm by pre-training a transformer on synthetic datasets sampled from a prior over functions, enabling in-context learning on new tabular datasets during a single forward pass.
- **Components**:
  - Synthetic data generator (Structural Causal Models)
  - Transformer architecture with row and column attention
  - In-context learning engine
- **When to use**: For any tabular classification or regression task, especially on small to medium-sized datasets where rapid deployment and zero hyperparameter tuning are desired.
### Do-PFN
- **How it works**: Extends PFNs to causal inference by generating training data from sampled structural causal models, simulating interventions, and learning to predict interventional targets.
- **Components**:
  - Causal graph sampler
  - Intervention simulator
  - Transformer inference network
- **When to use**: When estimating causal effects and predicting the consequences of interventions from observational data.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Nick Erickson applied TabPFN-3.5 to the 2015 Kaggle Otto Group Product Classification Challenge retrospectively.
- **Illustrates**: The power of tabular foundation models on historical competitive benchmarks.
- **Lesson**: TabPFN secured the #1 ranking solution in 1 line of code and 1 minute of compute, beating 3,500 teams.
### Hitachi applied TabPFN to predict maintenance workflows across Spain's railway network.
- **Illustrates**: Real-world industrial deployment of tabular foundation models.
- **Lesson**: Achieved significant maintenance cost savings and better workforce planning.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Use TabPFN for tabular classification and regression to skip hyperparameter tuning.
  - Integrate TabPFN with AI agents using Model Context Protocol (MCP).

## Notable Quotes
